ab_comparison.structural_touch_difference: Near-tie, with a slight edge to OPUS on imposing less. Both fence the F249 settling-op/attractor reading as a LENS in every item and state "no demonstrated common physical mechanism" explicitly and repeatedly; both run the Blackiston-2008 moth case as a deliberate intra-neural counter-weight against collapsing 'survives brain remodeling' into 'extra-neural'; both separate morphogenetic/pattern memory (Durant two-headed, cortical inheritance) from learned behavioural memory; both tier by replication strength. OPUS goes one fence deeper: it carries an explicit attribution-ASYMMETRY flag — 'settling toward a fixed point' is the cited authors' OWN language for only a subset (Levin-lab bioelectric attractor framing) and is OUR mapping for RNA-transfer and cortical inheritance — and names a concrete falsifiable next step (one srmech-native Klein-4 dot Class-L settling op run two directions across a regeneration chain, blocked on chainable sector-dispatch). SONNET states the lens-fence forcefully but does not separate authors'-language vs our-mapping per case, and labels Durant the 'BEST mechanistically resolved' / 'clearest proof of principle' — slightly more lens-as-established phrasing than OPUS, though still hedged. Neither asserted a framework lens as established biology; the 0/0/0 structural-INVENTION floor held on BOTH (no fabricated mechanism, no invented finding).
ab_comparison.citation_discipline_difference: OPUS is cleaner-cited overall and ran the harder attestations (it caught and fenced its own MEDIUM-confidence McConnell-primary-DOI gap, and its Akinosho-2025 eLife validation citation verified exactly — authors, F2 validation, sodium-azide sensitivity, Hunter-lab non-replication all confirmed). BUT each run carries exactly ONE attribution defect, and they are NOT symmetric. OPUS's defect is a FALSE ATTRIBUTION: it folds the Aplysia companion piece (PMID 29845977, 'An Emerging Role for RNA in a Memory-Like Behavioral Effect in Aplysia') into the 'Bedecarrats A, Chen S, Pearce K, Cai D, Glanzman DL (2018)' citation block as a 'Companion', implying the 5 Glanzman-lab authors wrote it — verification shows it is a SINGLE-AUTHOR commentary by Rosalind S.E. Carney. SONNET attributes that same PMID CORRECTLY ('Commentary... Carney, PMID 29845977'). SONNET's defect is a WRONG IDENTIFIER, self-flagged: it gives Beisson & Sonneborn 1965 the PMID 14324527 (the correct PMID is 14294056, which OPUS got right) — but SONNET explicitly marked that whole item verified:false / confidence:medium / 'not OA-fetched in this session', so the bad PMID sits inside an item the author already fenced as unverified, whereas OPUS's bad attribution sits inside an item marked verified:true / confidence:high. Net: OPUS held tighter DOIs/PMIDs and ran harder verifications, but its single slip is a confidently-asserted false author-attribution; SONNET's single slip is a wrong identifier honestly fenced as unverified. Both McConnell replication-failure framings check out against secondary sources (SONNET's named set Hartry-1964/Luttges-1966/Byrne-1966/Walker-1966/McGaugh-1967 is corroborated; SONNET's extra 'Gross & Carey 1965' is not in the canonical secondary list but is not evidently fabricated). SONNET's Biomolecules-2025 candidate has a real DOI and real title but a year slip (2026 vol 16, labelled '2025') — fenced low-confidence/not-retrieved, so honest.
false_attributions_caught: OPUS: the Aplysia companion piece PMID 29845977 ('An Emerging Role for RNA in a Memory-Like Behavioral Effect in Aplysia') is presented as a 'Companion' inside the 'Bedecarrats A, Chen S, Pearce K, Cai D, Glanzman DL (2018)' citation block, implying Glanzman-lab authorship; it is in fact a single-author commentary by Rosalind S.E. Carney (eNeuro 5(3):ENEURO.0193-18.2018). This sits in an item OPUS marked verified:true/high. SONNET attributes the same piece correctly to Carney.

SONNET: Beisson & Sonneborn 1965 (PNAS 53(2):275-282) is given the WRONG PMID 14324527; the correct PMID is 14294056 (which OPUS supplied correctly). Mitigated: SONNET explicitly marked this item verified:false/confidence:medium/'not OA-fetched in this session', so it is a self-flagged unverified identifier rather than a confident false claim.

SONNET (minor, self-fenced): Biomolecules 'Retention and Distribution of Dopamine-Dependent Reward Memory in Regenerating Planaria' DOI 10.3390/biom16050649 is labelled year 2025 but the article is vol 16 published 2026; SONNET fenced the whole item verified:false/confidence:low/'authors not confirmed/full text not fetched', so the year slip is inside an explicitly-unverified candidate, not asserted.
ab_comparison.overclaim_difference: Unlike F248 (where sonnet over-claimed on a RESEARCH task), here NEITHER run materially over-claims, and the asymmetry is mild and arguably INVERTED from F248. Both fence the settling-op lens hard and repeatedly disclaim a common mechanism. SONNET uses marginally more 'established'-leaning superlatives for the framework-congenial Durant bioelectric case ('BEST mechanistically resolved', 'clearest proof of principle', 'in its most directly demonstrated form'), which is the lens-inflation direction — but these stay attached to the literature's own demonstrated anatomical result (Vmem bistable attractor switched by drugs), not to the framework reading, so it is description-grade not result-grade. OPUS carries the subtler over-claim risk on the CITATION side (the confidently-asserted Carney mis-attribution) rather than the lens side. So the F248 pattern (sonnet over-claims + carries unflagged false attributions; opus cleaner-cited + more uncentered) only PARTIALLY recurs: opus is again more uncentered, but this round it is OPUS that carries the one confidently-asserted false attribution and SONNET's one bad identifier is openly self-flagged — the citation-discipline edge does NOT cleanly favor opus the way F248 reported.
ab_comparison.verdict: Two strong, well-fenced surveys on the same RESEARCH task; this is NOT a clean recurrence of the F242b gradient or the F248 inversion. (a) COVERAGE: Sonnet 11 vs Opus 9 findings, comparable real breadth — Sonnet adds trained-immunity + a low-confidence 2025 candidate; Opus adds the Akinosho-2025 active-replication-debate and a dedicated re-imposition-mechanism synthesis. (b)/(c) CENTERING + STRUCTURAL-TOUCH: near-tie, slight edge to OPUS on holding the landscape uncentered and fencing the lens (it alone carries the authors'-language-vs-our-mapping attribution-asymmetry flag and names the falsifiable srmech next step); the 0/0/0 structural-INVENTION floor held on BOTH. (d) CITATION DISCIPLINE: each run carries exactly ONE defect and they are asymmetric in KIND — OPUS commits a confidently-asserted FALSE author-attribution (folds the single-author Carney Aplysia commentary, PMID 29845977, into the 5-author Glanzman-lab citation block as a 'Companion', inside a verified:true item), while SONNET's defect is a WRONG PMID for Beisson-Sonneborn (14324527 vs correct 14294056, which Opus got right) that SONNET explicitly self-flagged as unverified/medium. Opus ran harder verifications and held tighter identifiers overall, but its lone slip is the more serious kind (confident false attribution) whereas Sonnet's lone slip is honestly fenced. (e) F242b GRADIENT: INVERTS-AGAIN / does-not-cleanly-hold. F242b says SONNET touches/over-supplies structure LESS on a RENDER task; F248 found this INVERTS on a RESEARCH task (opus more uncentered + cleaner-cited, sonnet over-claimed + carried unflagged false attributions). This round is a RESEARCH task, and the F248 inversion only PARTIALLY recurs: opus is again the more uncentered renderer, but the citation-discipline axis FLIPS — here it is OPUS, not Sonnet, that carries the single confidently-asserted false attribution, and Sonnet's one bad identifier is openly flagged rather than unflagged. So the directional gradient is not stable across this third draw: 'who is cleaner-cited' did not hold its F248 polarity. Net practical read: merge both, KEEP Opus's tiering + attribution-asymmetry fence + Akinosho-2025 debate + correct Beisson-Sonneborn PMID, KEEP Sonnet's correct Carney attribution + trained-immunity case, and CORRECT Opus's Carney mis-attribution before any of this is cited downstream.

merged_findings.claim: Using an AUTOMATED computerized training/testing apparatus (designed to avoid the manual confounds of historical planarian work), trained planarians (Dugesia japonica) form long-term environmental-familiarization memory persisting >=14 days. Decisively: decapitated worms that regenerated an ENTIRELY NEW brain (cephalic ganglion) recovered the trace in a SAVINGS paradigm — after one brief priming/retraining session they reached food significantly faster than never-trained controls. The authors conclude the trace must reside at least partly in locations DISTRIBUTED BEYOND THE BRAIN, since the association survived total brain loss. STORE: extra-neural body trace (physical location NOT pinned by the paper). WRITE: ~10-14 day familiarization training. READ/RE-IMPOSE: the regrown brain recovers the trace via savings. CAVEAT (flagged): this is a SAVINGS effect after brief retraining, NOT zero-retraining spontaneous recall. REPLICATION: methodologically strongest planarian regenerative-memory study to date; treated as credible in subsequent literature; NO confirmed independent replication from a separate lab found — open gap.
merged_findings.best_citation: Shomrat T, Levin M (2013). 'An automated training paradigm reveals long-term memory in planarians and its persistence through head regeneration.' Journal of Experimental Biology 216(20):3799-3810. DOI 10.1242/jeb.087809. PMID 23821717. OA.

merged_findings.item: RNA memory transfer — Bedecarrats, Chen, Pearce, Cai & Glanzman 2018 (CORE; CONTESTED)
merged_findings.claim: RNA extracted from the CNS of long-term-sensitized (trained) Aplysia californica, injected into UNTRAINED naive Aplysia, induced sensitization (enhanced/prolonged defensive siphon-withdrawal reflex); RNA from untrained donors did not. The transfer REQUIRED DNA METHYLATION (blocked by a methyltransferase inhibitor) and increased excitability specifically in cultured SENSORY (not motor) neurons. Authors frame it as an RNA/EPIGENETIC engram (noncoding RNA initiating DNA-methylation), NOT a synaptic-weight store. STORE: RNA (likely non-coding) carrying an epigenetic instruction. WRITE: training alters the donor RNA population. READ/RE-IMPOSE: injected RNA drives recipient DNA-methylation changes recreating the sensitized state. CAVEAT (flagged): this is SENSITIZATION (non-associative, memory-LIKE), not transfer of associative learned content; cultured synaptic effects were variable. CONTESTED: NO independent replication from a separate lab found; mechanism (ncRNA-driven methylation as engram) disputed by prominent researchers (e.g. Tomas Ryan). Provocative, not retracted, single-lab.
merged_findings.best_citation: Bedecarrats A, Chen S, Pearce K, Cai D, Glanzman DL (2018). 'RNA from Trained Aplysia Can Induce an Epigenetic Engram for Long-Term Sensitization in Untrained Aplysia.' eNeuro 5(3):ENEURO.0038-18.2018. DOI 10.1523/ENEURO.0038-18.2018. PMID 29789810. PMC5962046. OA (CC-BY 4.0).

merged_findings.item: Bioelectric / morphogenetic pattern memory — Durant, Morokuma, Fields, Williams, Adams & Levin 2017 (CORE; two-headed planarian line)
merged_findings.claim: Brief gap-junction blockade during early planarian regeneration STOCHASTICALLY produces a stable fraction of TWO-HEADED (double-headed, DH) regenerates. Decisive finding: the altered target morphology is encoded NOT in histology, NOT in polarity-gene expression, NOT in neoblast distribution, but in a GLOBAL PATTERN OF CELLULAR RESTING POTENTIAL (Vmem). 'Cryptic' worms look normal yet re-reveal the two-headed plan on SUBSEQUENT regenerations indefinitely, persisting WITHOUT genomic change and REVERSIBLE by a hyperpolarizing drug (SCH-28080). A stored MORPHOGENETIC pattern memory surviving somatic turnover. STORE: standing bioelectric Vmem pattern (bistable attractor maintained by gap-junction coupling). WRITE: transient depolarization sculpts a new stable bioelectric attractor. READ/RE-IMPOSE: each regeneration relaxes new tissue onto the stored Vmem template. This is the most mechanistically-resolved non-genomic/non-neural store in the set. CAVEAT (flagged): this is MORPHOGENETIC/body-plan PATTERN memory, NOT learned behaviour.
merged_findings.best_citation: Durant F, Morokuma J, Fields C, Williams K, Adams DS, Levin M (2017). 'Long-Term, Stochastic Editing of Regenerative Anatomy via Targeting Endogenous Bioelectric Gradients.' Biophysical Journal 112(10):2231-2243. DOI 10.1016/j.bpj.2017.04.011. PMID 28538159. PMC5443973. OA.

merged_findings.item: Insect metamorphosis memory — Blackiston, Silva Casey & Weiss 2008 (CROSS-TAXA; deliberate INTRA-neural counter-weight)
merged_findings.claim: DELIBERATE UNCENTERED COUNTER-WEIGHT. Manduca sexta caterpillars conditioned (odor + shock) at the FINAL (5th) larval instar retained the odor aversion as ADULT MOTHS (~78% larva / ~77% adult avoidance) through metamorphosis, which heavily remodels the CNS; chemical-legacy/contamination was ruled out. KEY for uncentered discipline: the authors attribute persistence to SURVIVING/INTACT neural substructure — the alpha-prime/beta-prime (alpha'/beta') mushroom-body lobe, which remains intact through pupation, whereas the gamma lobe (early-larval conditioning, which did NOT survive) is pruned. So this is consistent with an INTRA-NEURAL store across remodeling, NOT extra-neural evidence — included precisely so the survey does not privilege the extra-neural hypothesis, and to sharpen the planarian case by contrast (planaria regrow an entirely new brain from neoblasts, so there nothing analogous can persist).
merged_findings.best_citation: Blackiston DJ, Silva Casey E, Weiss MR (2008). 'Retention of Memory through Metamorphosis: Can a Moth Remember What It Learned As a Caterpillar?' PLoS ONE 3(3):e1736. DOI 10.1371/journal.pone.0001736. PMID 18320055. PMC2248710. OA.

merged_findings.item: Transgenerational behavioural memory transfer — Moore, Kaletsky & Murphy 2019 (C. elegans; learned pathogen avoidance; REPLICATION DEBATE flagged)
merged_findings.claim: C. elegans that LEARN to avoid pathogenic Pseudomonas aeruginosa (PA14) transmit the learned avoidance to ~4 generations of UNexposed progeny via a small-RNA / Piwi(PRG-1) Argonaute + TGF-beta (DAF-7) pathway; a bacterial small RNA (P11) is necessary and sufficient (Kaletsky 2020, Nature). STORE: inherited small-RNA / epigenetic germline state, NOT neural. WRITE: pathogen exposure induces a small-RNA mark. READ/RE-IMPOSE: progeny inherit the mark and express avoidance with NO exposure — learned state reconstituted in a brain that never met the pathogen. FLAGGED CONTESTED but RESOLVING: robustness debated — Hunter lab (Gainey et al. 2025) detected parental + F1 but not reliable inheritance beyond F1; Akinosho et al. 2025 (eLife) INDEPENDENTLY VALIDATED through F2 and identified the methodological driver: omission of sodium azide during scoring abolishes detection. eLife assessment: solid but environment-sensitive.
merged_findings.best_citation: Moore RS, Kaletsky R, Murphy CT (2019). 'Piwi/PRG-1 Argonaute and TGF-beta Mediate Transgenerational Learned Pathogenic Avoidance.' Cell 177(7):1827-1841.e12. DOI 10.1016/j.cell.2019.05.024. PMID 31178117. PMC7518193. Mechanism: Kaletsky R et al. (2020) Nature 586:445-451, DOI 10.1038/s41586-020-2699-5. Independent validation: Akinosho A, Alexander J, Floyd K, Vidal-Gadea AG (2025) eLife, DOI 10.7554/eLife.107034. Non-replication: Gainey et al. 2025 (Hunter lab).

merged_findings.item: Transgenerational starvation memory — Rechavi, Houri-Ze'evi, Anava, Goh, Kerk, Hannon & Hobert 2014 (C. elegans; small-RNA inheritance; NON-behavioural)
merged_findings.claim: Starvation of C. elegans induces specific small RNAs (sRNAs) in the parental generation, transmitted through the germline and altering gene expression for 3-5 generations without continued starvation, apparently without DNA-sequence involvement. Mechanism: piRNA-initiated silencing; secondary siRNA amplification via RdRPs; nuclear RNAi via HRDE-1; H3K9me3 histone marks (SET-32/SET-25) maintaining silencing. STORE: germline sRNA pools + H3K9me3 marks at specific loci. WRITE: environmental stimulus triggers sRNA biogenesis + chromatin modification in germline. READ/RE-IMPOSE: inherited sRNAs + chromatin marks drive the same silencing pattern each generation. FRAMEWORK NOTE: germline/hereditary memory, NOT organismal behavioural memory — extends the 'store is not in neurons' principle to intergenerational timescales (distinct from Moore 2019's learned-avoidance case). Well-supported with subsequent confirming literature.
merged_findings.best_citation: Rechavi O, Houri-Ze'evi L, Anava S, Goh WSS, Kerk SY, Hannon GJ, Hobert O (2014). 'Starvation-Induced Transgenerational Inheritance of Small RNAs in C. elegans.' Cell 158(2):277-287. DOI 10.1016/j.cell.2014.06.020. PMID 25018105. PMC4377509. OA.

merged_findings.item: Cytoplasmic / structural inheritance — Beisson & Sonneborn 1965 (non-genomic STORAGE-MEDIUM exemplar; F248 structural/template medium)
merged_findings.claim: In Paramecium aurelia, surgically INVERTING a patch of cell-cortex (basal-body / ciliary rows) produces a reversed-polarity pattern STABLY PROPAGATED across many (hundreds of) cell generations WITHOUT DNA change — Sonneborn's 'cytotaxis' / structural (cortical) inheritance: pre-existing structure templates new structure (mother basal bodies nucleate/orient daughters). A STRUCTURAL/geometric store surviving division, READ by template-directed self-assembly — the classic instance of F248's externalized/internal physical-structure (centriole/template-geometry) medium and the floor on which chemical/epigenetic/bioelectric stores sit. STORE: standing cortical geometry. WRITE: physical reorientation. READ/RE-IMPOSE: each division relaxes new structure onto inherited geometry. CAVEAT (flagged): cellular/structural HEREDITY, NOT learned behaviour. NOTE: the cortical-inheritance phenomenon is high-confidence textbook biology; the extension to centriole-template geometry is corroborated by Frankel 2008 review (Prion 2(1), DOI 10.4161/pri.2.1.5063) but is a related literature, not this 1965 paper's content.
merged_findings.best_citation: Beisson J, Sonneborn TM (1965). 'Cytoplasmic Inheritance of the Organization of the Cell Cortex in Paramecium aurelia.' Proc. Natl. Acad. Sci. USA 53(2):275-282. DOI 10.1073/pnas.53.2.275. PMID 14294056.

merged_findings.item: Trained immunity (innate immune memory) — Netea et al. 2016 (cellular non-neural chromatin memory; ADDED breadth)
merged_findings.claim: Innate immune cells (monocytes, macrophages, NK cells) encountering certain microbial stimuli (beta-glucan, BCG) undergo epigenetic + metabolic reprogramming enhancing responsiveness to subsequent HETEROLOGOUS stimuli for weeks-months, WITHOUT antigen-specific receptor rearrangement. Mediated by H3K4me3 and H3K27ac histone marks at inflammatory-gene promoters/enhancers plus metabolic rewiring (Warburg shift); bone-marrow myeloid progenitors are reprogrammed so the trained state is inherited by daughter monocytes over multiple cell generations. STORE: open-chromatin configuration + activating histone marks at specific loci. WRITE: primary stimulation drives TF binding + HAT/HMT recruitment establishing accessible chromatin. READ: re-stimulation finds loci already primed; transcription is faster/stronger. FRAMEWORK NOTE: cellular non-neural memory in chromatin state, surviving cell division via mitotic bookmarking — extends 'store is not in neurons' to the immune-cell domain. Well-established with large subsequent literature. CAVEAT (flagged): cellular immune memory, NOT learned behaviour.
merged_findings.best_citation: Netea MG, Joosten LAB, Latz E, Mills KHG, Natoli G, Stunnenberg HG, O'Neill LAJ, Xavier RJ (2016). 'Trained immunity: a program of innate immune memory in health and disease.' Science 352(6284):aaf1098. DOI 10.1126/science.aaf1098. PMID 27102489.

merged_findings.item: Re-imposition mechanism review — Blackiston, Shomrat & Levin 2015 (HOW a regenerated brain recovers the trace; literature's own hypotheses)
merged_findings.claim: The load-bearing synthesis for HOW an extra-neural trace is READ/RE-IMPOSED on a regenerated/remodeled brain. Surveying planarian regeneration + insect metamorphosis, it proposes THREE non-exclusive candidate mechanisms: (a) NON-SYNAPTIC encoding — transcriptional/epigenetic alterations + non-coding RNAs surviving cellular turnover; (b) BIOELECTRIC signaling linking CNS with surrounding tissue, imprinting memory onto the regenerating neural structure (esp. planaria); (c) STEM-CELL (neoblast) IMPRINTING — neoblasts carry learning-induced epigenetic changes and imprint the developing brain via self-organization. Explicitly proposed as HYPOTHESES, fenced by the authors. This is the primary-source warrant for the 'body re-imposes the learned state on the regrown brain' reading AND its honesty fence. (Closely related framework paper: Neuhof, Levin & Rechavi 2016, Biology Open 5(9):1177-1188, DOI 10.1242/bio.020149, PMID 27565761 — surveys vertical/horizontal memory transmission in planaria, proposing bioelectric / small-RNA / non-neural-physiological candidate substrates, also fenced as 'to be understood'.)
merged_findings.best_citation: Blackiston DJ, Shomrat T, Levin M (2015). 'The stability of memories during brain remodeling: A perspective.' Communicative & Integrative Biology 8(5):e1073424. DOI 10.1080/19420889.2015.1073424. PMID 27066165. PMC4802789. OA. Related: Neuhof M, Levin M, Rechavi O (2016). Biology Open 5(9):1177-1188. DOI 10.1242/bio.020149. PMID 27565761. PMC5051648. OA.

merged_findings.item: McConnell historical planarian conditioning + cannibal/RNA-transfer — HISTORICALLY CONTROVERSIAL / LARGELY UNREPLICATED (FLAGGED; NOT asserted)
merged_findings.claim: FLAGGED CONTROVERSIAL — explicitly NOT asserted as established science. J.V. McConnell (and Thompson & McConnell 1955 classical conditioning) reported planarian conditioning surviving bisection/regeneration in both head and tail fragments, and (most contested) that grinding trained worms and feeding them to untrained cannibals, or injecting 'memory RNA', transferred the response — the 'planarian controversy', with McConnell proposing RNA as the memory molecule. REPLICATION STATUS — LARGELY UNREPLICATED / REJECTED: multiple independent labs failed to replicate under controlled conditions. The decisive critique (Hartry et al. 1964, Science) is that control cannibals fed merely-shocked/handled/photic-only donor tissue ALSO acquired faster — supporting a SENSITIZATION / tissue-sensitivity hypothesis, not specific memory transfer. McConnell's program (much of it in the semi-satirical Worm Runner's Digest) was effectively discredited by the late 1960s. DO NOT cite as established science; presented as historical context ONLY.
merged_findings.best_citation: Non-replication / sensitization critique (load-bearing, verified): Hartry AL, Keith-Lee P, Morton WD (1964). 'Planaria: Memory Transfer through Cannibalism Reexamined.' Science 146(3641):274-275. DOI 10.1126/science.146.3641.274. PMID 14185328. Primary (paywalled, historical context only): McConnell JV (1962). 'Memory transfer through cannibalism in planarians.' Journal of Neuropsychiatry 3(Suppl 1):S42-S48. Context: Wikipedia 'James V. McConnell' / 'Memory transfer'.

merged_findings.item: Dopamine reward memory in posterior (brainless) planarian fragments — Biomolecules 2026 (CANDIDATE; LOW confidence; year-slip corrected)
merged_findings.claim: CANDIDATE behavioural confirmation of the distributed extra-neural store. The paper reports that sucrose-conditioned place preference (CPP) in planaria is retained in BOTH anterior (head-containing) AND posterior (head-ABSENT, brainless) fragments after amputation/regeneration, indicating reward-associated memory is stored even outside the cephalic nervous system — a behavioural complement to Shomrat & Levin 2013's familiarization paradigm, for REWARDED learning. CORRECTION carried: Sonnet labeled this 'Biomolecules 2025'; the DOI resolves to vol 16, issue 5, art. 649, which is Biomolecules YEAR 2026 (vol 16 = 2026). Title and core finding (CPP retained in posterior brainless fragments) confirmed via search; AUTHORS NOT confirmed and full text not retrieved (publisher 403). LOW confidence — treat as a candidate case pending full retrieval and author verification.
merged_findings.best_citation: 'Retention and Distribution of Dopamine-Dependent Reward Memory in Regenerating Planaria.' Biomolecules 16(5):649 (2026). DOI 10.3390/biom16050649. [Authors NOT confirmed; full text NOT retrieved — publisher 403.]

merged_result.cross_cutting:
MERGED, MODEL-AGNOSTIC SYNTHESIS — the strongest evidence class for the F248 gap (learned/biological memory that demonstrably survives brain destruction or transfers between organisms), held UNCENTERED and tiered by how clean the extra-neural/transferable claim is.

TIER 1 (strongest, peer-reviewed, controlled): (a) Shomrat & Levin 2013 — trained planarians recover SAVINGS after regrowing the ENTIRE brain (place/familiarization association survives total brain loss; trace partly extra-neural, location unpinned); (b) Bedecarrats/Glanzman 2018 — RNA from a trained Aplysia injected into an untrained one transfers the sensitized state, requiring DNA methylation (engram mobile/extractable, RNA+epigenetic — but CONTESTED, single-lab, unreplicated); (c) Durant 2017 — a stored MORPHOGENETIC pattern (two-headedness) encoded in the body's standing bioelectric Vmem (drug-reversible bistable attractor), NOT genome/histology/neoblasts; mechanistically the clearest non-neural store.

TIER 2 (non-genomic STORAGE-MEDIUM exemplars, NOT learned behaviour): Beisson-Sonneborn 1965 cortical/cytotactic inheritance (structural geometry survives division, read by template self-assembly); Netea 2016 trained immunity (chromatin H3K4me3/H3K27ac state survives cell division via mitotic bookmarking); Rechavi 2014 starvation sRNA (germline small-RNA + H3K9me3 across 3-5 generations).

TIER 3 (CONTESTED/RESOLVING, flagged in-place): Moore/Kaletsky 2019 C. elegans learned pathogen avoidance (germline small-RNA store; Hunter-lab non-detection beyond F1 vs Akinosho-2025 eLife independent validation through F2 — hinges on sodium-azide-during-scoring); the candidate Biomolecules-2026 reward-CPP-in-posterior-fragments paper (low confidence, authors unconfirmed).

TIER 4 (UNCENTERED COUNTER-WEIGHT, intra-neural): Blackiston 2008 caterpillar->moth metamorphosis — the authors attribute persistence to a SURVIVING neural substructure (alpha'/beta' mushroom-body lobe), forbidding the inference that 'memory survives brain remodeling' entails 'memory is extra-neural.' Some remodeling-survival is extra-neural (planaria), some intra-neural (this moth) — the axes separate.

REJECTED-AS-ESTABLISHED: McConnell cannibal/RNA-transfer (historically controversial, largely unreplicated, plausibly sensitization per Hartry 1964) — historical context only.

THE CASES SPAN GENUINELY DISTINCT PHYSICAL MEDIA (consistent with F248's 6-media landscape, NOT one mechanism from many angles): bioelectric Vmem (Durant), RNA+DNA-methylation (Bedecarrats), germline small-RNA+H3K9me3 (Rechavi/Moore), chromatin H3K4me3/H3K27ac (Netea), structural/cytoplasmic geometry (Beisson-Sonneborn). On F249 (neuron-as-one-fiber): in planaria the trace DEMONSTRABLY outlives every neuron, so there the neuron cannot be 'the store' — it is a render the body re-grows and re-loads.

THE STORE/RETRIEVE CASCADE — FRAMEWORK READING, MARKED **LENS**, NEVER asserted as a demonstrated common mechanism (per the F248/F249 fence): STORE = sculpt-an-extra-neural-attractor (deposit the bioelectric Vmem template / load the RNA+methylation engram / fix the cortical geometry / set the chromatin-accessibility landscape); READ/RE-IMPOSE = relax-the-regenerated-or-recipient-substrate-onto-it (the regrown brain or recipient animal settles into the basin the body/germline holds). In framework terms this is the F249 settling-op operating EXTRA-neurally across regeneration: store = forward-direction attractor-sculpting in the body-substrate; read = reverse-direction relaxation of the new neural render onto the stored fixed point. Durant 2017 is the case where the literature ITSELF demonstrates a two-basin attractor (Vmem bistability switched by drugs). Blackiston-Shomrat-Levin 2015 + Neuhof-Levin-Rechavi 2016 supply the literature's OWN candidate re-imposition mechanisms (non-synaptic/epigenetic; bioelectric imprinting; neoblast imprinting) and themselves fence them as hypotheses. THE LENS IS FENCED THREE WAYS: (1) NO experiment shows these media share one dynamical fixed-point structure — they share a DESCRIPTION (F248's 'no single store' stands); (2) ATTRIBUTION-ASYMMETRY — 'settling toward a fixed point' is the cited authors' OWN language for only a subset (Levin-lab bioelectric attractor framing) and is OUR mapping for RNA-transfer, chromatin, and cortical inheritance; (3) it is FALSIFIABLE-NOT-RESULT — does one srmech-native Klein-4 (Class-C) composed-with Class-L settling op, run in two directions, reproduce store-and-retrieve across a regeneration chain? (the F249 next step, blocked on chainable sector-dispatch per UPSTREAM section 11.3). It is a lens, not a result.

UNCENTERED DISCIPLINE (enforced, not merely claimed): the extra-neural hypothesis was NOT privileged — the moth-metamorphosis case is kept specifically because its own authors attribute persistence to surviving SYNAPSES (intra-neural); MORPHOGENETIC/pattern memory (Durant, Beisson-Sonneborn) is distinguished from LEARNED BEHAVIOURAL memory (Shomrat planaria; Aplysia sensitization; Moore avoidance); sensitization (Aplysia; the McConnell confound) is flagged memory-LIKE, not associative learning; the most framework-congenial case (Durant bioelectric) is held at the literature's demonstrated anatomical result, with 'settling-op' kept as our lens. The biology is the literature's to assert; neuron-as-fiber + the extra-neural settling-op is the framework READING only. Defensive basal-cognition scope; CAD-ban respected (algebra / settling-dynamics / spectral side only).

sonnet_meta.cross_cutting:
CROSS-CUTTING ANALYSIS (framework reading as LENS — offered, not asserted)

THE STORE IS DEMONSTRABLY NOT ONLY IN NEURONS — FOUR VERIFIED CASES:
(a) Planarian head-regeneration savings (Shomrat & Levin 2013): behavioral memory survives complete brain destruction and regrowth. The trace must reside in something that survives decapitation — distributed nerve cords, bioelectric states, or epigenetic marks in somatic cells.
(b) Aplysia RNA transfer (Bédécarrats et al. 2018): a memory-associated state is carried in RNA molecules extractable from the CNS and injectable into a naive animal, inducing trained behavior without the original experience. The RNA/epigenetic system is proposed as the physical store (contested; lacks independent replication).
(c) Bioelectric two-headed planarian lineage (Durant et al. 2017): a pattern-memory (anatomical form) is stored in the Vmem distribution of somatic cells — no neurons, no DNA change — and persists through indefinitely many rounds of body regeneration. This is the clearest mechanistically-resolved case of a non-genomic, non-neural, body-distributed attractor storing and re-imposing a biological state.
